newsitem.title: USA: Oregon optimistic on Enron, Portland merger.
newsitem.headline: Oregon optimistic on Enron, Portland merger.

text.p: The staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) said Monday it is optimistic it will be able to recommend the merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Corp, but it will delay formal comment until next Tuesday, April 29.
That is the previously-scheduled day for all interested parties to submit their comments on the merger to the OPUC.
Last week, Enron submitted a revised merger plan to the staff, which included $141 million in rate cuts for Oregon electricity customers.
The OPUC staff had previously recommended rejection of the $2.1 billion merger unless customer benefits of $141 million were guaranteed.
"We are optimistic that staff will be able to recommend merger approval," said Phil Nyegaard, OPUC administrator, financial analysis division, in a statement.
Oral arguments before the commission are slated for May 6, and a final decision by the three-member OPUC is expected on June 4.
